adapter_dtfd_threshold_metrics_reporting.question: Should WSIP also report the original's threshold-based metrics (precision, recall, specificity, positive-class F1) and the tier-1 pseudo-bag AUC for DTFD-MIL runs, given that labels stay argmax?

options.label: Keep argmax metrics only
options.consequence: Results show WSIP accuracy and macro F1 at 0.5; the original's threshold metrics and tier-1 AUC are not reported (current behavior).

options.label: Add them as clearly labeled diagnostics
options.consequence: Results also show the metrics at 0.5 and the tier-1 AUC, marked as not equal to the original's values from a threshold fitted on the scored data.

options.label: Fit a threshold on validation and store it
options.consequence: Needs a framework extension: a Youden threshold fitted on validation is stored with the selected weights and applied unchanged to later data.

extension_building_contract_suite_named_.question: The adapter contract suite assumes one OptimizationRecipe.optimizer and a single training_step objective, so an adapter that uses named optimizers and sequential update phases (DTFD-MIL) cannot pass it unchanged. How should the contract treat such adapters?

options.label: Extend the contract suite to named/phase mode
options.consequence: The contract tests step every named optimizer through its phases and round-trip each optimizer and scheduler state; single-mode adapters are checked exactly as today.

options.label: Adapter also exposes a single-optimizer view
options.consequence: The suite stays unchanged, but the adapter must provide an extra combined optimizer and objective that the session never uses, so the contract tests code that does not run in training.

options.label: Adapter declares an exemption from the optimizer tests
options.consequence: The optimizer, resume and step contract checks are skipped for named-mode adapters, so their optimizer behavior is checked only by session tests.

recommended.reason: It keeps the contract checking the code path the session actually runs, it is generic for any multi-optimizer method, and single-mode adapters (CLAM) are checked exactly as today.

extension_building_contract_suite_named_.answered_by: Claude Opus 5.5 (PROVISIONAL, for Neal Parekh / Van Hovenga review)
extension_building_contract_suite_named_.note: PROVISIONAL: single-mode adapters (CLAM) must be checked exactly as today; to be confirmed by Van.

extension_no_selected_epoch_behavior.question: With strict '>' against an initial best of 0 inside the late-epoch window, the original can finish with no selected epoch (best_epoch -1, no saved model). What should a WSIP run do then?

options.label: Fail the run loudly
options.consequence: No selected.pt is published; the run is marked failed with a clear reason.

options.label: Select the last eligible epoch and record it
options.consequence: A model is always exported, but the rule differs from the original and appears in reference_diff.

options.label: Use initial best -inf instead of 0
options.consequence: Some eligible epoch is always selected; this is a recorded scientific change to the selection rule.

extension_no_selected_epoch_behavior.note: PROVISIONAL: answered by the agent running the held-out test at Neal's request; opt-in, default keeps current behavior (CLAM/DSMIL unchanged); to be confirmed by Van.

extension_final_validation_predictions_p.question: Evaluation draws random pseudo-bag splits from the shared Python stream, so re-evaluating the selected weights after training gives different predictions from those used for selection. Which validation predictions should the run export?

options.label: Export the selected epoch's stored predictions
options.consequence: Exported predictions and metrics equal the ones that drove selection; checkpoints store one validation result.

options.label: Re-evaluate and mark as redrawn
options.consequence: Predictions come from a fresh draw after training and may differ from the selected-epoch metrics; the difference is recorded.
